params.name: p.standstill_speed_max
params.convention: rest-detection resolution: the speed below which sampled position differences are indistinguishable from sensor noise at typical trace rates, so that the measurement counts as complete cessation from movement
params.source: vehicle-dynamics instrumentation practice for zero-velocity detection (zero-velocity update thresholds in odometry and INS literature)

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: stop-point tolerance: the distance from the required stopping place within which a halt counts as made at that place, set from stop-line placement and positioning accuracy
params.source: MUTCD stop-line placement practice together with map-matching position accuracy

params.name: p.intersection_view_sight_min
params.convention: intersection sight-distance model: the length of the intersecting approach that must be visible from the stopping place for a driver to see approaching traffic, computed for the intersecting way's prevailing speed and a driver's gap-acceptance time
params.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance (Case B, stop-controlled approach)

params.name: p.backing_speed_min
params.convention: rearward-motion resolution: the speed above which a measured velocity opposed to the heading is distinguishable from sensor noise at typical trace rates, so that the motion counts as motion
params.source: vehicle-dynamics instrumentation practice for zero-velocity detection

params.name: p.same_direction_cos_min
params.convention: heading-alignment tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle between headings still counted as the same direction, set to cover lane-keeping yaw and heading noise within a lane
params.source: trajectory-analysis practice for same-direction classification (about 18 degrees)

params.name: p.following_time_headway_min
params.convention: time-headway convention on a dry surface: perception-reaction time plus the margin by which a follower's braking distance must not exceed the leader's, expressed as a time multiplied by the measured speed
params.source: driver-behaviour and car-following literature; the two-second rule in driver training and highway capacity practice

params.name: p.following_time_headway_adverse_min
params.convention: time-headway convention on a degraded surface or in crowded traffic: the same stopping-distance model with the reduced friction coefficient of a wet, icy or snow-covered surface, and with the reduced escape room of dense traffic
params.source: stopping-distance models with wet and icy friction coefficients (AASHTO Green Book deceleration rates)

params.name: p.adverse_curvature_min
params.convention: curvature above which the highway's alignment restricts the view and the available friction enough to call for the adverse headway, taken from the minimum radius of a design speed in the highway range
params.source: AASHTO Green Book horizontal-curve design (a 250 m radius)

params.name: p.adverse_grade_min
params.convention: grade magnitude above which the slope changes braking distance enough to call for the adverse headway
params.source: AASHTO Green Book grade-corrected stopping-sight-distance tables

params.name: p.traffic_vicinity_range
params.convention: the reach within which other road users count as the traffic upon the highway about the subject, set from the length of road a driver is responding to at highway speed
params.source: traffic-flow practice for local density estimation over a road segment

params.name: p.traffic_crowded_count
params.convention: the number of road users within the vicinity range at or above which the traffic upon the highway counts as dense, so that the adverse headway applies
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual level-of-service density bands converted to a count over the vicinity range

params.name: p.caravan_min_count
params.convention: the number of other members, within the procession gap and travelling in the subject's direction, at or above which a close succession of motor vehicles counts as a caravan or motorcade rather than ordinary following
params.source: traffic-flow practice for platoon identification (platoon size thresholds in arterial progression studies)

params.name: p.caravan_member_gap_max
params.convention: the largest body gap within which two motor vehicles count as members of one close succession, taken from platoon headway criteria at highway speeds
params.source: platoon-identification practice (headway thresholds of about three seconds at highway speed)

params.name: p.procession_space_min
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the length of a design passenger vehicle plus a standing clearance at each end -- the space a vehicle must occupy at rest once it has entered the line
params.source: design-vehicle lengths and standing clearances (AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle, about 6 m, with about 2 m of clearance at each end)

params.name: p.procession_space_time_min
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the time headway an entering vehicle needs at the two ends of the space it occupies, taken together, multiplied by the measured speed of the line, so the required space grows with speed; about half a second at each end, the headway accepted at the small relative speeds of a merge into a line of traffic, and set so that a close succession within p.caravan_member_gap_max can still leave the required space at ordinary highway speeds
params.source: gap-acceptance studies for merging into a traffic stream (lag and gap acceptance at low relative speed; critical-gap practice in the Highway Capacity Manual)

params.name: p.motion_speed_min
params.convention: motion resolution: the speed above which a measured velocity is distinguishable from sensor noise, so that the road user counts as moving and so as being driven
params.source: vehicle-dynamics instrumentation practice for zero-velocity detection

params.name: p.direction_alignment_cos_min
params.convention: direction-agreement tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle between a road user's velocity and a region's designated direction still counted as travelling with that direction, set at a right angle so that any forward component counts as with the direction and only a component against it counts as against
params.source: trajectory-analysis practice for wrong-way detection (sign of the along-direction velocity component)

params.name: p.signal_lead_time
params.convention: signal-lead convention: the time before a lateral movement throughout which the indicator must have shown the side of the movement, taken from the lead time a following driver needs to perceive and react to the signal
params.source: driver perception-reaction time practice and jurisdictional signalling-distance rules converted to a time at urban speeds

params.name: p.lane_change_clearance_min
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the smallest clearance between bodies at which a lane change is accepted, and the closest approach the movement must leave within the horizon
params.source: lane-change gap-acceptance studies (minimum accepted clearances in naturalistic driving data)

params.name: p.lane_change_horizon
params.convention: the horizon over which the closest approach under the current velocities is computed for the movement, taken from time-to-collision practice for lane changes
params.source: surrogate-safety-measure practice (time-to-collision horizons for lane-change conflicts)

params.name: p.lane_change_time_gap_min
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the time gap a following vehicle in the target lane must retain, the body gap being required to be at least the closing speed multiplied by this time
params.source: lane-change gap-acceptance studies (critical time gaps for merging)

params.name: p.cautious_speed_max
params.convention: the cap on the speed of a cautious crossing of an uncontrolled conflict area: the crawl from which a vehicle halts within a few metres, above which no amount of visibility makes the crossing cautious
params.source: low-speed crawl conventions for restricted-visibility junctions (MUTCD/AASHTO guidance on stop-controlled and signal-failure operation)

params.name: p.cautious_clearing_time_max
params.convention: stopping-sight-distance model: the perception-reaction plus braking time within which the visible stretch of the intersecting way must be clearable, so that the permitted speed falls with the distance that can be seen
params.source: AASHTO stopping-sight-distance model (perception-reaction 2.5 s plus braking)

params.name: p.yield_clearance_min
params.convention: gap-acceptance and conflict-margin convention: the smallest clearance between the two bodies, at the closest approach their current velocities give, at which the subject counts as having granted precedence rather than proceeded in preference to the other; one design-vehicle width of lateral margin
params.source: surrogate-safety and critical-gap practice (TRB gap-acceptance studies; conflict-margin thresholds)

params.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
params.convention: the horizon over which the closest approach of two bodies under their current velocities is computed for a junction conflict, taken from time-to-collision conventions for intersection conflicts
params.source: surrogate-safety-measure practice (time-to-collision thresholds for intersection conflicts)

params.name: p.immediate_hazard_arrival_max
params.convention: critical-gap convention: the time for an approaching vehicle, at its measured speed, to reach the intersection, at or below which it is so close as to constitute an immediate hazard to a manoeuvre across its path; the critical gap for a left turn across opposing traffic
params.source: gap-acceptance practice (HCM critical-gap figures for permitted left turns; AASHTO intersection sight distance)

params.name: p.opposed_direction_cos_min
params.convention: direction-opposition tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed between two designated directions of travel, or between a designated direction and a road user's heading, still counted as opposite directions
params.source: lane-geometry tolerance practice (heading-alignment tolerances used for same-direction and oncoming tests)

params.name: p.turn_left_heading_change_min
params.convention: turn-recognition convention: the leftward heading change over the recognition window above which a course change counts as a turn rather than a curve of the road or a lane change
params.source: turning-movement geometry (AASHTO intersection turning paths)

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: the window behind the observation over which the heading change of a turn is integrated, taken from the duration of a turning movement at junction speeds
params.source: turning-movement duration practice (intersection operations studies)

params.name: p.yield_sign_approach_speed_max
params.convention: the speed at or below which an approach to a yield sign counts as “slowed” in the subsection's own words “slowed or stopped”: a walking-pace crawl at the place, from which a halt is immediate and from which the driver can take in the through highway
params.source: yield-sign approach practice (MUTCD yield-sign operation; low-speed crawl conventions)

params.name: p.reversal_heading_change_min
params.convention: reversal-recognition convention: the magnitude of heading change over the window above which the road user proceeds in the opposite direction, set below a half turn to allow for the alignment of the two directions of a way and for integration error
params.source: manoeuvre-recognition practice for U-turn detection in trajectory data

params.name: p.reversal_window
params.convention: the window behind the observation over which the heading change of a reversal is integrated, long enough to cover a reversal made in several movements as the definition allows
params.source: turning-path and multi-point-turn timing practice for design vehicles

params.name: p.centreline_proximity_max
params.convention: lane-width convention: the width, measured from the centreline, of the portion of the right half of the highway counted as nearest the centreline — one design lane width, so that on a two-lane two-directional road the single lane beside the line qualifies and on a wider road only the innermost lane does
params.source: AASHTO design lane width (12 ft)

params.name: p.standstill_yaw_rate_max
params.convention: rotation-detection resolution at rest: the rate of change of heading below which a sampled heading difference is indistinguishable from heading noise on a standing body, so that a measured rotation at or below it leaves the halt a complete cessation from movement
params.source: sensor-resolution practice for heading estimation of halted vehicles

params.name: p.approximately_same_time_window
params.convention: the largest interval between the two entry observations within which the entries count as made at approximately the same time: the critical gap practice uses for two conflicting approaches at an uncontrolled junction, within which the later entrant could not have cleared the conflict area before the earlier one arrived
params.source: critical-gap practice for uncontrolled intersections (HCM gap-acceptance figures)

params.name: p.curvature_resolution_min
params.convention: curvature-measurement resolution: the curvature magnitude at or above which a measured value is distinguishable from the zero of a straight alignment, taken from the lateral-position noise of a mapped centreline over one sampling interval; it states when a bend is measured at all and nothing about how sharp a bend must be
params.source: road-geometry surveying and map-matching error practice

params.name: p.crest_vicinity_max
params.convention: sight-distance model: the length of the approach to a crest within which the crest's vertical curve restricts the view ahead, taken from the stopping sight distance at highway speeds, so that a vehicle within that distance of the crest region is on the approach to or near it
params.source: AASHTO Green Book crest vertical curve and stopping sight distance tables

params.name: p.turning_yaw_rate_min
params.convention: yaw-rate resolution: the rate of change of heading at or above which a turning body is distinguishable from one holding a straight course, taken from the noise floor of a vehicle-grade yaw sensor
params.source: inertial-sensor specification practice

params.name: p.course_change_heading_min
params.convention: course-change recognition convention: the heading change over the recognition window at or above which a vehicle has turned from a direct course, set from the heading excursion of a single lane change at highway speed, so that a departure from a direct course short of a junction turn is recognized
params.source: lane-change kinematics studies

params.name: p.course_change_window
params.convention: the window behind the observation over which the heading change of a course change is integrated, taken from the measured duration of a completed lane change or junction turn at urban speeds
params.source: lane-change and turn duration measurements

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_base_max
params.convention: stopping-sight-distance model: the speed on a dry surface, full lane width, clear air and free flow at which the design stopping distance is still covered by the sight distance ordinarily available on an open highway; the base bound the other factors reduce
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance tables

params.name: p.wet_surface_speed_factor
params.convention: friction-reduction convention: the fraction of the dry-surface bound left by the reduced tyre-pavement friction of a wet surface, from the ratio of wet to dry braking distances
params.source: pavement friction and wet-weather speed studies

params.name: p.ice_surface_speed_factor
params.convention: friction-reduction convention for an icy or snow-covered surface: the fraction of the dry-surface bound left by the ratio of icy to dry braking distances
params.source: winter-maintenance friction measurements

params.name: p.precipitation_speed_factor
params.convention: the fraction of the clear-weather bound left while rain or snow is falling, from the measured reduction in sight distance and in available friction during precipitation
params.source: adverse-weather speed and visibility studies

params.name: p.darkness_speed_factor
params.convention: the fraction of the daylight bound left by headlamp-limited sight distance in darkness, from the low-beam illuminated distance against the stopping distance
params.source: night-driving sight distance practice

params.name: p.steep_grade_speed_factor
params.convention: grade-braking convention: the fraction of the level-road bound left where the slope lengthens the braking distance, from the grade-corrected stopping distance formula
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping distance on grades

params.name: p.crowded_traffic_speed_factor
params.convention: the fraction of the free-flow bound left where other members of the traffic are close enough that their manoeuvres bear on the subject, from the speed-density relation of a crowded stream
params.source: traffic-flow speed-density relations

params.name: p.nominal_lane_width
params.convention: design lane width: the width at and above which the lane imposes no reduction on the bound; below it the bound falls in proportion to the measured width
params.source: AASHTO Green Book lane width standards

params.name: p.clearing_time_min
params.convention: stopping-distance model: the perception-reaction plus braking time within which the vehicle must be able to halt inside the distance it can see, so the bound is that distance divided by the time, written as a product
params.source: AASHTO Green Book perception-reaction and braking times

params.name: p.lateral_acceleration_max
params.convention: side-friction convention: the lateral acceleration a curve may impose on the vehicle at the bound, from the comfortable side-friction factors of horizontal curve design
params.source: AASHTO Green Book side friction factors

params.name: p.following_lateral_offset_max
params.convention: same-line-of-travel tolerance: the largest offset across the subject's heading, between the two vehicles' reference points, within which the two travel in one line of travel, set at half the width of a standard lane so that a vehicle in the line beside the subject lies beyond it while a vehicle offset within its own line lies within it
params.source: AASHTO Green Book lane widths (a 3.6 m lane) and design-vehicle widths

_fields.params: name (p.<name>), value (number), unit (m|s|m/s|m/s2|deg|deg/s|ratio|count), convention (text), figure_review (optional: why a value that equals a figure some law states is a convention, not that figure)
_fields.aggregates: word (a legal aggregate such as 'vehicle'), classes (ru.* ids it covers)

declarations.meaning: The place the road user occupies at the observation lies outside any business district: no territory contiguous to and including the highway there is declared, for this map or trace, to have buildings in use for business or industrial purposes occupying the frontage a business district requires. The source declares it per map or per trace; where it is not declared, the fact is unknown.

The source's current plan for the road user is to turn to the left at the target region: the declaration is true where that plan includes a left turn there, false where the plan decides otherwise for that target (another manoeuvre, passing through, a left turn cancelled or already completed), left out where the plan does not decide it, and absent where the source has no plan for that road user at that target. It follows the source's declaration and not the road user's motion, so a left turn that is blocked, delayed or under way stays true while the plan holds it.

The place the road user occupies at the observation lies within a business or a residential district: the territory contiguous to and including the highway there is declared, for this map or trace, to have buildings in use for business or industrial purposes, or dwellings or dwellings combined with such buildings, occupying the frontage such a district requires. The source declares it per map or per trace; where it is not declared, the fact is unknown.
